name: distributed-lock-job-dedup-p1
prompt: how do I stop two workers from running the same scheduled job at the same time

chunks.content: we run three worker replicas, each with its own cron, which is why a nightly job sometimes fires more than once
the worker uses a pool of eight threads so it can process several queue messages in parallel
jobs are picked off a Redis list and acknowledged only after they finish successfully
the transfer runs inside a single database transaction so the debit and credit either both commit or both roll back
every job run logs its job id and replica name so we can tell which worker did what
the cron expressions were normalized to UTC after a daylight-saving shift caused a job to skip a day
before doing any work each replica tries to acquire a single named lock; only the holder proceeds and the others exit immediately, guaranteeing one runner
the lock carries an expiry plus a monotonically increasing token, so if a holder stalls past the TTL a slow zombie cannot still write after another worker has taken over
alternatively we elect a single leader replica that owns all scheduled work, and followers stay idle until the leader's lease lapses
transient failures retry with jittered backoff up to five times before alerting
set a container memory limit and the workers restart cleanly when they approach it
the bulk CSV import streams rows instead of loading the whole file into memory
regenerated the OpenAPI spec so the docs page reflects the new endpoints
